purpose: Stable field IDs, paths and types for future attribute/filter consumers; no query execution or weighting.

fields.definition: Excitement and visceral exhilaration during viewing.
Suspense, dread, or anticipation of an uncertain outcome.
Fright or horror experienced, independently of horror genre membership.
Sense that characters face harm, including harm never shown.
Romantic affection or longing evoked in the viewer.
Erotic atmosphere or sexual tension, independently of explicit sexual depiction.
Affectionate, kind, or emotionally welcoming tone.
Reassurance through care, kindness, and emotional safety.
Awe, amazement, or fascination with discovery.
Acute pity, sorrow, or tragic emotional impact.
Lingering, reflective sadness.
Unease from the strangely familiar or almost natural.
Emotional release after accumulated tension or feeling.

Optimistic outlook or belief in positive possibilities.

Overall strength of emotional engagement, regardless of positive or negative tone.
Sustained pressure, discomfort, or anxiety experienced during viewing.
Encouragement, joy, or improved spirits evoked.
Invitation to reflect on ideas, ethics, or interpretations beyond the immediate plot.
Light, mischievous, or freely inventive tone.
Overt appeal to tender feelings and emotional attachment.
Understated expression and withholding of overt emotional display.
Positive and painful feelings intertwined rather than merely appearing separately.
Experience of incongruity, illogic, or strangeness, whether humorous or unsettling.
Immersion away from everyday concerns; not limited to fantasy settings.
Invitation to imagine desired powers, relationships, status, or ways of life.
Calm, restful or meditative feeling evoked; not merely absence of tension.
Moral outrage or righteous anger evoked in the viewer; distinct from anger depicted by characters.
Revulsion evoked, independently of comic gross-out, frightening threat or grotesque visual style.
Overall amount and strength of comedy, independently of individual humor styles.

Humor from verbal cleverness, puns, or linguistic ambiguity.
Humor from bodily action, slapstick, or visual physical mishaps.

Humorous imitation of a recognizable work, genre, or style.
Humor about death, suffering, taboo, or tragedy.
Recurring jokes whose repetition or variation creates humor.
Humor about storytelling, production, audiences, or the work itself.
Humor delivered with apparent seriousness or minimal emotional reaction.
Humor relying on bodily fluids, disgust, or vulgar physical material.
Sexually explicit or bawdy humor; distinct from noncomic sensuality and nonsexual gross-out humor.
Criminal acts and their consequences as subject matter.
Uncovering an important unknown as a central concern.
Armed conflict and its human or societal consequences.
Governance, political institutions, and struggles for political power.

Examination or criticism of social arrangements and norms.

Explicit thematic exploration of what humans are like: capacities, impulses, morality, cooperation, cruelty, or tensions between nature and social conditioning. Ordinary human characters, emotion, or drama alone is insufficient; not a synonym for personal identity, consciousness, or existential meaning.
Religious belief, spiritual practice, or metaphysical meaning.

A supernatural entity inhabits or takes control of a person as a horror mechanism. Explicitly excludes psychological dissociation, an alternate personality without supernatural inhabitation, ordinary manipulation or influence, and merely owning or using a magical object.

A supernatural entity inhabits or takes control of a person. Psychological dissociation, alternate personality without supernatural inhabitation, mere influence, and owning a magical object do not qualify.
Transformation, violation, or instability of the body matters to the horror.
Folk belief, ritual, landscape, or insular tradition matters to the horror.
Human insignificance before incomprehensible forces matters to the horror.
Perception, mental distress, or internal instability drives the horror.

Use of environmental sound to create atmosphere.

Use of little or no non-diegetic score.

Sound that acknowledges or plays with the work's representational frame.

How consistently focal characters demonstrate effective practical, professional or intellectual skill in consequential tasks. Distinct from intelligence, claimed expertise, power, luck or training merely occurring. Zero means no demonstrated competence, not an unintelligent person. Assess the depicted performance; competence_basis separately records how skill is established.

Demand for retaining and retrieving names, relationships, clues and earlier details over the assessed work to follow it. Distinct from sustained attention, plot complexity or knowing other installments. Assess an attentive first-time viewer who understands the presentation language; do not assume a particular memory impairment.

Demand for working out unstated motives, causal connections or events to follow the work. Distinct from optional deeper interpretation, thematic thought provocation or deliberately unresolved ambiguity. A simple plot may still require substantial inference. Assess an attentive first-time viewer who understands the presentation language.

Rate at which consequential new information arrives and must be processed to follow the work, in speech, images or sound. Distinct from total exposition, dialogue quantity, cutting speed and the pace of physical action. Repetition and rapid movement without new information do not by themselves increase this demand.

Ease of regaining the narrative thread after a brief distraction or viewing break without rewinding. Assume a first-time viewer who understood the work up to that point and understands its presentation language. Reorientation cues and intelligible scene goals can help. Distinct from continuous background viewing or joining midway without prior context. Higher means easier recovery, not a greater demand; this is a work-level tendency, not a promise for every interruption or viewer.

Perceptual prominence of depicted dance performance or dance sequences across the assessed work, including social, stage, ritual and imagined dance. Independent of dancing's narrative centrality, dance skill or choreography quality. Singing alone, dance-music accompaniment, rhythmic editing and combat choreography do not establish dancing. Zero means no perceptibly featured dancing; a supported fleeting dance can be a trace.

Extent to which a protagonist or co-protagonist is characterized and motivated through earlier traumatic experiences. Trauma elsewhere in the story, a single tragic fact or ordinary unhappiness does not establish dependence. Assess narrative emphasis, not a clinical diagnosis. Selections across character fields need not describe the same protagonist.

Magnetism or persuasive personal appeal displayed by protagonists/co-protagonists toward others or through their presentation. Distinct from attractiveness, morality, actor popularity, competence and acting quality.
Prominence of idiosyncratic, unconventional habits and behavior among substantial characters. Not inferred from disability, neurodivergence, nationality or mere outsider status.

Occult or esoteric ceremonies, invocation or ritual practices matter to the work, whether their supernatural effects are real, ambiguous or disbelieved. Ordinary religious observance alone does not qualify; do not label unfamiliar cultures occult.

Social or geographical insulation of a community from outsiders matters to the story. A rural location, secret organization or physically isolated individual alone does not establish an isolated community.
Sustained creeping apprehension of an ominous threat, including quiet stretches. Distinct from abrupt startles, brief fear, action urgency, general sadness and simply withholding information.
Perceptual emphasis on natural landscapes or scenic built surroundings across the work. Not production location, setting centrality or an automatic judgment of beauty.

Strength of audiovisual cues evoking physical environmental sensations such as dampness, heat, cold, air, surfaces and texture. Distinct from general immersion, emotional intimacy, extreme weather and merely being set outdoors.

Recurrence of deliberately staged abrupt startles over the assessed work. Zero means assessed no jump scares; 1 is an isolated rare startle, 5 recurring intermittently, 10 pervasive repetition. Not a scene count, intensity score or artistic-quality judgment. Unknown remains null.

Strength of progressive intensification in stakes, consequences or conflict across substantial narrative arcs. Distinct from constant high stakes, fast pace, twist count or increasing darkness. A work may escalate without plot twists.

Extraordinary personal abilities beyond ordinary human capability matter to the work, in or outside combat. Superhuman abilities of nonhuman focal characters also qualify; ordinary expertise, technology used as a tool or monsters merely existing does not by itself qualify.

Monstrous beings or creatures are a focus of the work, whether threatening, sympathetic or ambiguous. Nonhuman identity or an animal alone does not establish a monster; do not apply this to human social groups.
Tracking, pursuing, capturing or eliminating supernatural beings drives substantial activity. Excludes ordinary wildlife hunting and merely encountering, fleeing or befriending supernatural beings.

Substantial presentation patterns within scope; select every pattern actually used. Chronological and reverse-chronological strands can coexist. Occasional memories do not establish interleaved timelines; a repeated time loop alone is not reverse chronology. Non-temporal applies to substantial passages not organized by story time.

Ways substantially the same events are presented again from different accounts. Parallel storylines alone do not qualify. Complementary accounts add information; conflicting accounts disagree. Select both when both occur; [] when assessed with neither.

Substantial tone patterns within scope, not an exact timeline or a claim about every episode. Select multiple directions if different arcs use them. Broadly stable applies to substantial stable stretches; alternating tones means repeated switching. Comedy and horror blended throughout do not alone establish comic_to_horror.
How focal characters' demonstrated skill is established. These are whole-work categories, not claims that all tags describe the same person. Do not equate intelligence with competence.

Sources of narration or explanatory speech, excluding ordinary dialogue. First-person character narration does not imply direct audience address. Source recordings are retained historical/archival speech rather than newly added explanation.
Abrupt audiovisual events deliberately staged to startle. General fear, loudness or sustained tension alone is not a jump scare.
Modalities used by actual jump scares, independently of sound-design prominence. Empty only when assessed absent; null when undetermined.
Recorded or live audience laughter included in the soundtrack; ordinary characters laughing is excluded.
Extended or repeatedly sustained screaming in the soundtrack, distinct from an isolated shout or startle.

Functions of scenes during or after credits within the assessed edition. Select all that apply, including multiple functions in one scene. [] means no qualifying scene/functions; null means undetermined. A comic tag need not reopen a threat.

Recurring case/problem resolution patterns in the assessed episodes. Select all substantial patterns; [] when there is no case/problem structure. Not cancellation status, ending quality or a promise about unseen seasons.

Substantial continuity patterns for character relationships/development across the assessed episodes. Resetting some strands and developing others can coexist. Independently assessed from case resolution.

Substantial depicted story eras, not production dates. A brief mention or prop does not establish a setting. Ancient/medieval are broad temporal labels, not a claim that all societies share one historical periodization.
Substantial story periods relative to the title's original release, not today. Multiple selections describe the work overall, without pairing each period to an event.
Kinds of depicted reality that matter to the work. Physical staged reality (e.g. an elaborate set) is distinct from a digital simulation or virtual reality.
Environmental conditions that materially impede action or survival. Scenic weather alone does not qualify; these tags do not identify who is obstructed or when.
Substantial seasons depicted, based on the setting's local climate/calendar. Release month and viewing associations are insufficient.
Named celebrations actually depicted or materially organizing the story. This bounded vocabulary is not exhaustive; do not invent a new label for an unlisted tradition.

Established artistic affiliation or substantial recognizable stylistic tradition. Country, language, slow pacing or production date alone is insufficient. This list is bounded; unlisted traditions require a future schema revision, not a guessed synonym.

Social/cultural experiences substantially depicted, independently of the production industry or an actor's identity. Diaspora and indigenous contexts require established depiction, not inference from appearance.

Explicitly established traits of one or more protagonists/co-protagonists. Whole-work set: selections need not describe the same person. Never infer from an actor's identity, appearance, name or a viewer stereotype. Adult means established adulthood and can overlap older_adult; do not infer age from the performer.
Substantial production methods used. Select both for live-action/animation combinations; ordinary CGI visual effects alone do not make a live-action work animated.
Modes used in substantial passages; select fiction and nonfiction for an explicit hybrid. A fictional mockumentary is fiction, not nonfiction merely because it imitates a documentary.
Show formats used within scope. Limited describes a deliberately bounded run and can coexist with episodic, serialized or anthology structure. Not current release/cancellation status.
Substantial color presentation modes in the assessed edition. Select color and black_and_white if both occur; tinting can coexist with an underlying monochrome image.

Source-material types contributing substantially. Multiple sources may coexist; original refers to substantial independently originated material, not every small adaptation change. Do not invent source-work identifiers.
Relationships to real people/events within scope; multiple selections may apply. Disputed is supported factual controversy, not the model being unsure. No selection certifies accuracy.
Animation techniques actually used, not creatures depicted. Select each substantial technique instead of a generic mixed tag.
Observable presentation modes, not audience approval.
Devices used in documentary-style presentation, including fictional mockumentary. Voiceover origin is captured separately.

Known original capture media, never inferred from a digital streaming release or merely simulated grain. Select each known medium. Null when undetermined; do not guess components from a mixed-format label.
Known relation types to other works; these tags do not resolve target works or establish influence from resemblance alone.
Affiliation with the anime production/artistic tradition; animation alone is insufficient.
Principally silent-film/intertitle presentation, not simply sparse dialogue.
Whole work presented as one continuous take, real or simulated; an isolated long take is insufficient.
Main narrative is presented approximately in real elapsed time; not merely rapid plot events.
A scene during/after credits in this edition, not ordinary credit text.
Known alternative endings for this title/edition; do not invent them from narrative ambiguity.

Recognizable dance styles actually depicted in the assessed work, independently of narrative importance. Select all supported styles, including overlaps. Do not infer a style from soundtrack genre, production country, costume alone or combat movement. Broad folk_traditional is not a claim about a particular named tradition; other means a known depicted style outside this bounded vocabulary. Null means the styles cannot be assessed; [] means no listed style identified, not certified absence of all dancing.

Contexts in which dancing is actually depicted. Select all supported contexts; styles and contexts are whole-work sets and need not describe the same sequence. Narrative musical number includes imagined or expressive dance, not singing alone. Stage performance is different from everyday social dancing; rehearsal is not automatically competition. Null means undetermined; [] means no listed context identified.

Sustained visually dominant on-screen colors, from grading, lighting, costumes or design. Exclude a single prop or fleeting image, posters and assumed symbolism. Multiple selections need not appear together; black/white/gray describe tonal dominance, not automatically monochrome presentation.

Substantial on-screen palette relationships, regardless of production technique. Monochromatic means a narrow hue family, not necessarily black-and-white. Analogous uses neighboring hues; complementary uses opposing hues; selective_color isolates colors against subdued/monochrome surroundings; changing_palettes requires substantial palette shifts.

Substantial established motives of protagonists/co-protagonists, not every action or an inferred diagnosis. Whole-work set; wealth and power need not motivate the same person. Revenge is not automatically a tragic-backstory dependence.

Sustained behavior of protagonists/co-protagonists. Cunning means strategic guile; manipulative means steering others through calculated influence; ruthless means willingness to disregard others welfare for an aim. Self_destructive means repeatedly acting against own welfare. These do not follow automatically from competence, antihero status or identity. Tags may describe different leads.

Substantial protagonist patterns, not inferred from a single mood or scene. Social_alienation is estrangement/exclusion; accumulated_frustration is sustained mounting dissatisfaction; destructive_rebellion is resistance through damaging or destructive acts. They need not co-occur in one protagonist. Other arc attributes remain independently assessed.

Kinds of substantially depicted organized groups. Militant requires endorsement or use of combative/coercive force in pursuit of aims, not merely strong beliefs. Ideological describes organizing shared doctrine; political describes political aims. Secrecy, religion, ethnicity or outsider unfamiliarity alone does not establish militancy or coercion.

Sustained focal perspectives through which an organized group is encountered: newcomer joins or enters its world; journalist investigates/reports; undercover conceals investigative identity; visitor remains outside; insider depicts established membership; defector leaves. Whole-work selections need not concern the same group or character.

Substantially depicted internal group processes. Operational_methods means showing how a group pursues its aims; mere group presence is insufficient. Select only established processes, not stereotypes about the group type.

Substantial dynamics within depicted friendships: mutual care, recurring friction, attempted repair, enabling harmful choices, and unresolved strain. Repair does not imply success or complete resolution. Different tags may concern different friendships; not an assertion of realism or overall ending closure.

Substantial romantic relationship dynamics: concealment, social disapproval, public scandal or conflicting loyalties. Secrecy is not necessarily shame or infidelity; disapproval needs depiction, not the assessor judging identities. Whole-work tags need not concern the same romance.

Substantial perceptible weather/atmospheric conditions, whether scenic or obstructive. Humid requires cues of damp heavy air; tropical geography or rain alone does not establish humidity. Do not infer conditions solely from season, production location or a storm-related plot reference.

Substantial depicted qualities of built surroundings. Old_historic denotes visibly/established older structures; decaying denotes deterioration, independently of age, poverty, haunting or visual beauty.

Broad real-world geographical story settings substantially depicted, not filming locations, production countries, character ancestry or travel aspirations. Transregional stories can select multiple. Fictional or unidentified geography stays untagged/unknown rather than guessed; this bounded field does not supply country-level precision.

Sources with substantial audible environmental presence, independently of narrative importance. Do not infer audible sound from visible objects or setting. Natural ambience can be designed or recorded; this makes no recording-technique claim.

Kinds of threatened or actual animal harm depicted or explicitly referred to. Deliberate_cruelty denotes intentional abuse or torment, including neglect; it is distinct from an accidental injury or natural death. Threats can coexist with cruelty. Different tags need not concern the same animal. Unknown parent presence requires null; assessed absent parent requires []; none of these are independently verified exclusion guarantees.

Main substantial story eras by narrative emphasis. Multiple selections require genuinely balanced major timelines; a brief flashback is insufficient. Select only eras also assessed in world_context.eras. Unknown remains null.

Substantial established story decades, not release decades. Bounded vocabulary 1800s–2190s; other periods use eras/year bounds. [] means no listed decade identified, not timelessness. Do not guess from production date, a prop or a brief flashback.

Main story decades by narrative emphasis; multiple when major timelines are balanced. Each selection must also be in depicted_decades. Outside the bounded vocabulary use eras/year bounds, not the nearest decade. Unknown remains null.

Earliest established calendar year of substantial depicted story settings. Signed historical years: -1 means 1 BCE, 1 means 1 CE; no year zero. Not release date, a fleeting flashback, an inferred exact date from broad era labels, or a promise that all intervening years are depicted. Null if that boundary cannot reasonably be established, including undated prehistoric/fantasy settings. Boundaries can be independently unknown.

Latest established calendar year of substantial depicted story settings. Signed historical years: -1 means 1 BCE, 1 means 1 CE; no year zero. Not release date, a fleeting flashback, an inferred exact date from broad era labels, or a promise that all intervening years are depicted. Null if that boundary cannot reasonably be established, including undated prehistoric/fantasy settings. Boundaries can be independently unknown.
